question:
As shown below, convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) has sides \(AB=3,\) \(BC=4,\) \(CD=6,\) \(DE=3,\) and \(EA=7.\) The pentagon is originally positioned in the plane with vertex \(A\) at the origin and vertex \(B\) on the positive \(x\)-axis. The pentagon is then rolled clockwise to the right along the \(x\)-axis. Which side will touch the point \(x=2009\) on the \(x\)-axis?

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_10B_Q13_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Because the pentagon is convex, clockwise rolling places its sides on the axis in the repeating order \(AB,BC,CD,DE,EA\). Each new side starts where the preceding side ends and extends right by its unchanged length. Thus one complete cycle covers
\[
3+4+6+3+7=23
\]
units, after which the same arrangement repeats farther right.

Now
\[
2009=87\cdot23+8.
\]
So we need the side covering the position 8 units into a cycle. Within a cycle, \(AB\) covers positions 0 to 3, \(BC\) covers 3 to 7, and \(CD\) covers 7 to 13. Since \(7<8<13\), the point lies inside the interval covered by \(\overline{CD}\), giving choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
